name: Davis Conservation Foundation grants
summary: Twice-yearly, normally one-year grants to 501(c)(3) charities working on wildlife, wildlife habitat and environmental protection, with highest priority on Northern New England (the Northern Forest and Gulf of Maine) and a preference for projects involving volunteers and communities.
reporting: A completion report is due at the project's end date or within one year of receiving funds.

eligibility.rule: Have a primary purpose related to environmental protection and conservation
Located in New England, or impact and spending kept mainly in priority areas (rare exceptions)
If an outdoor recreation organization, be primarily focused on environmental or outdoor stewardship
Not for individuals, annual giving, deficit reduction, scholarships, fellowships, loans or travel

documents: 501(c)(3) letter, if received in the last 24 months
Latest financials: audit, or Form 990 with balance sheet and income statement

calls.label: Twice-yearly rounds (April 1 and October 1)
calls.recurring: Applications are due online by 5:00 p.m. on April 1 and October 1 each year.

status.quote: April 1 and October 1. Applications must be submitted online by 5:00 p.m. on the deadline date.

recurring.quote: April 1 and October 1. Applications must be submitted online by 5:00 p.m. on the deadline date.

applicant_types.quote: The Foundation supports 501(c)(3) charitable organizations devoted primarily to wildlife, wildlife habitat, environmental protection and outdoor recreation.

access.quote: Applications are accepted only though our online application system.

window.quote: April 1 and October 1. Applications must be submitted online by 5:00 p.m. on the deadline date.

reporting.quote: Yes, a completion report is due at a project's end date or within one year of receiving funds.

effort.quote: The Foundation is only able to accept requests through our online portal.

eligibility.quote: A. Tax Exempt: 501(c)(3) classified as 509(a)(1) or (2).
Eligible organizations must have the primary purpose related to this vision.

C. Located in a Geographic Priority Area (listed in order of priority): Northern Forest and Gulf of Maine Northern New England (Maine, NH, VT) Other New England (low priority) Few organizations from outside of New England receive grants. In rare exceptions, projects may be approved if their impact and expenditure of funds will primarily be contained within geographic priority areas.
Outdoor recreation organizations that are not primarily focused on environmental/outdoor stewardship
Individuals, annual giving campaigns, deficit reduction, scholarships, fellowships, loans, or travel.

after_award.quote: 12 months from their award letter date, grantees are required to submit a completion report.

documents.quote: Your 501c3 letter (only if your organization received its letter within the last 24 months) Your project budget Most recent financials, provided as EITHER A or B A: the audit for your most recent fiscal year B: Your most recent 990, and your most recent FY balance sheet, and your most recent income statement Your current year operating budget
